subject: FinSight: SDK prioritized-queue header ignored — field ask + exception request
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
To: dev_patel@redwood.com, logan_wright@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 6 Nov 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: FinSight: SDK prioritized-queue header ignored — field ask + exception request

Folks,

Quick context: FinSight (large POC, FS-2028-1174) is seeing their low-latency paths (small inference requests for embeddings + short-chat queries) being routed into bulk queues despite setting the new x-redwood-priority: high header from our SDK. They reported tail latency spikes during business hours which are blocking their go-live next week.

Attached: reproduction steps (finsight_repro_steps.txt) and a trace log that shows the header arriving at the gateway but not being honored (priority-header-trace-20281106.log).

Ask: can runtime/platform team do a short investigation to confirm whether there is a routing header race in the SDK->gateway handshake? If there's a quick mitigation (hotfix or temporary policy exemption to route FinSight to the dedicated low-latency pool), they need it urgently.

Customer priority: high. Tara (FinSight) said they can accept a temporary route change + confirmation that we won’t regress. Pricing/credits TBD — looping in Kar for approval.

Can we get:
- quick triage note by EOD today (what's seen in the logs)
- if confirmed, an expected timeline for a canary hotfix or a routing policy override

Thanks — tagging Logan for Sales-Eng context and Marissa for on-call coordination.

— Ava
Ava Chen
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
ava_chen@redwood.com

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: ava_chen@redwood.com, logan_wright@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 6 Nov 2028 11:19:00 -0800
Subject: Re: FinSight: SDK prioritized-queue header ignored — field ask + exception request

Thanks for the signal and logs, Ava. I pulled the trace. Preliminary notes:

- The x-redwood-priority header is appearing at the edge (see log line 342) but I see cases where the router does a downstream header merge where priority can be lost if the request is retried during handshake. That matches a race we've seen in dev experiments (edge retry + header map).
- I opened SUP-2345 with the minimal repro included.

Immediate mitigation options we can do in the short term:
1) Policy override: create a tenant-based routing exception to force FinSight requests to the low-latency pool. This is quick (config push), limited blast radius — ETA ~2–3 hours and no code change.
2) Hotfix: fix the header propagation race in the router (requires a patch, CI, and canary). Rough ETA 2–4 days depending on release queue.
3) SDK-side workaround for FinSight: send a secondary metadata field (x-rd-priority-fallback) inside body metadata so the gateway can fallback if header is missing. Requires a small SDK patch and customer opt-in — ETA ~3 days for a canary build.

Next steps I recommend: do option (1) now to get them stable, then run the router hotfix pipeline (option 2) to permanently remove the race.

I'll attach the SUP-2345 link in the thread and will mark it P0.

— Dev
Dev Patel
Senior Software Engineer, Runtime

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: ava_chen@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com, logan_wright@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 6 Nov 2028 12:01:00 -0800
Subject: Re: FinSight: SDK prioritized-queue header ignored — field ask + exception request

Appreciate the quick triage, Dev. Confirming customer impact:
- Tara (T. Lim) reported 400–700ms tail for small chat calls (expected <80ms) during 10am–2pm ET windows.
- They are mid-POC and will sign Dedicated if we can guarantee stable low-latency across their 50 qps profile.

On mitigation: please do the tenant-based routing override (1) ASAP — FinSight agreed to the temporary routing change. I'll coordinate the customer side and validate after the change.

On credits: Kar, they want us to commit to a 1-week SLA exemption window and test results before we talk commit pricing. Recommend we prepare a short exec note because this will likely be escalated.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Principal Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ava_chen@redwood.com, logan_wright@redwood.com
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 6 Nov 2028 13:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: FinSight: SDK prioritized-queue header ignored — field ask + exception request

Thanks team — keep me posted. A few quick decisions:
- Approved: tenant-based routing override as an exception for FinSight for up to 7 days while we validate post-mitigation behavior. Marissa, please confirm scope (all endpoints vs selected routes).
- Approve a discretionary credits hold if we see repeated regressions after override — we'll finalize amount after post-mitigation metrics.
- If Dev's hotfix ETA is 2–4 days, prioritize a canary on a subset of nodes to validate without broad exposure.

Marissa: please get Tara's permission in writing for the temporary redirect (we need customer approval for routing exceptions). Logan: can you prepare a short external-facing note that explains the mitigation and next steps for the FinSight execs? Keep it non-technical for procurement.

— Kar
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales Ops, Redwood Inference

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: tara@finsight.ai, samir@finsight.ai
Cc: ava_chen@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 8 Nov 2028 17:42:00 -0800
Subject: Quick update: temporary routing exception + next steps (FinSight)

Tara / Samir — looping you in with our internal plan and timelines.

Summary of action taken:
- We verified your trace and confirmed a header propagation race in the runtime router. We've applied a tenant-scoped routing override to send FinSight traffic to the low-latency pool. This change is live as of 17:15 PT and we are monitoring.

What to expect now:
- Short-term: we expect tail latency to return to target within the hour for the routes you pointed out. Marissa will validate with your team.
- Medium-term: runtime team (Dev) will roll a canary hotfix to fix header propagation across retries (ETA 2–4 days).
- We will follow-up with a short post-mortem and a proposed credit if there is measurable impact once we finish validation.

If this plan looks good, please reply with a quick acknowledgement ("OK to proceed") so we have written approval for the temporary redirect.

Thanks — we’ll keep this short and make sure the change is minimally disruptive.

— Logan
Logan Wright
Group Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: proposal_v3.pdf (routing-exception-notes, optional post-mortem template)
